- Support for committed monthly token buckets with quarterly true-up (preferred) vs. annual true-up.

Sam —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attachment. High level: yes, we can support a flexible committed model that includes both a step-down discount ladder and a hurdle-based rebate; we have standard playbooks for quarterly true-up and a few optional rider credits for ramp/PoC.

Key bullets (summary):
- Commit structure: monthly committed tokens (SKU'd). Customer can choose 12/24/36-month term. Quarterly true-up (default) with option for monthly smoothing for enterprise accounts.
- Step-down discount ladder: tiered unit-prices that reduce at pre-agreed thresholds (example tiers: 0-100M, 100M-500M, 500M+ tokens). Ladder applies to committed bucket usage first.
- Hurdle rebate: we support a two-hurdle model — a lower hurdle (H1) that guarantees a protected price; if actual usage in a quarter is between H1 and commit, customer qualifies for a small rebate credit (applied to next invoice). If usage is above commit we charge overage at the applicable burst rate.
- Ramp credits: we can offer a one-time ramp credit (e.g., 10–25% of month 1 usage cost) depending on commit and term.
- Technical discounts: additional 8–15% off base per-token rates for customers that use offline batching/kv-caching and pin to quantized variants.

I'll attach a draft pricing table (redwood-pricing-table.xlsx) with sample numbers and a short explanation of reconciliation logic. Can we hop on a 30-minute call Tuesday to walk through the mechanics and which tiers you want to model?

Proposed next steps:
1) Call Tues 10:00 PT to review table and identify target commit bands.
2) We’ll supply a written commercial response + example MOA with reconciliation clauses.
3) Procurement issues PO or requests edits; legal reviews SLA exceptions.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-table.xlsx (xlsx)

Sam / Mina —

Quick technical note to support the commercial mechanics:

- How we meter: tokens are counted at the inference gateway (per-request tokens in/out). We can expose per-model family metering (e.g., base vs. capable family) if you want separate buckets.
- Hurdle detection: we compute monthly usage and aggregate to quarter for reconciliation. Hurdle rebates are implemented as ledger credits; we can apply them to the next invoice or hold as prepaid credits depending on procurement preference.
- Burst handling: reserved capacity (Dedicated) customers can attach burst cushion; if burst is consumed beyond reserved pools we charge overage at the burst rate defined in the table. Overage calculation: P50 concurrency billing for sustained excess and per-token for short spikes.
- Constraints: rebate and ramp credits cannot be combined with marketplace reseller pricing; quantized-variant discounts require model pinning and may change latency SLOs — include in MOA.

I've annotated redwood-pricing-table.xlsx with technical callouts. Happy to diagram how the quarterly true-up runs for your procurement and show GL-like amortization for ramp credits.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Commercial term sheet: Finovate Bank (draft) — commit + hurdle rebate + ramp credit

Sam —

Please find a concise commercial term sheet below (attached as MOA draft and pricing xlsx). Summary of agreed items:

- Commit: 24-month term; customer to select a monthly committed token quantity (proposal scenario: 250M tokens/month).
- Pricing ladder (illustrative):
  • 0–100M: $0.00160 / token
  • 100M–500M: $0.00120 / token
  • 500M+: $0.00095 / token
- Hurdle rebate: Quarterly reconciliation. Lower hurdle (H1) = 70% of committed monthly volume. If quarterly realized usage is between H1 and committed volume, Finovate receives a rebate equal to 10% of the price difference between H1 pricing and ladder-applied pricing (credit applied to next invoice). Credits may roll forward up to one subsequent quarter.
- Ramp credit: One-time credit equal to 20% of month 1 invoice if customer signs 24-month term and commits >=250M tokens/month. Credit applied as invoice credit within 30 days.
- Overage/burst: Per-token overage = $0.00275/token for short spikes; sustained above-commit usage billed using P50 concurrency rules; options to add Dedicated capacity for burst cushion.
- Discounts: Additional technical discount (8%) available if customer adopts quantized model variants and pins behavior for the contract term.
- Legal/SLAs: Any SLA exceptions and marketplace-reseller adjustments must be negotiated as addenda; non-standard terms will require legal review.

Attachments: proposed-moa-draft.docx (docx), redwood-pricing-table.xlsx (xlsx)
